To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

- The CMS dataflow is well understood by the Spanish CMS computing community, and the sites have developed and implemented the necessary software to handle the CMS dataflows and to provide the necessary services to the CMS community.
the CMS dataflows and data processing and analysis workflows can be successfully exercised in the Spanish Tier-2 sites and that the dataflows and workflows are stable and reliable.

CMS dataflows and analysis workflows have been exercised in computing challenges at Spanish Tier-1 and Tier 2 centres, and that these exercises are useful to validate and improve CMS data transfer, processing, analysis and data storage operations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of data transfer and processing performance in the CMS computing system.

the following topics: 1) Data transfer: we have studied the data transfer performance of the Spanish Tier-2 sites, and have developed a data transfer tool that can be used to optimize data transfer operations.

the study of data transfer and processing strategies, the development of tools for the management and analysis of CMS data and the optimisation of data analysis workflows in the context of CMS computing challenges.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Spanish Tier-2 sites are now able to perform the CMS computing operations in a fully independent and self-contained way.
the sites are prepared for the CSA07 challenge, with the only exception of the CIEMAT-Madird Tier-2 centre, where a new computing farm is currently being deployed.
the Spanish sites have demonstrated their ability to perform at the level required by the CMS computing model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been successful in exercising the dataflows and workflows for CMS physics data processing and analysis at the Spanish Tier sites.
we have been able to exercise and validate the full data flow from the Tier-0 to the Tier-2 sites and to the user community, and to exercise and validate our analysis and simulation software.

we have exercised the full data transfer, processing, analysis and storage capabilities of our sites and that we have been able to provide CMS with the required computing and analysis resources for their challenge.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the CMS data processing and analysis operations at the Spanish Tier sites have been successfully tested and validated, and that the sites have been fully prepared to face the upcoming challenges of the LHC era.
a significant fraction of the computing resources at the Spanish sites can be used for CMS data processing and analysis, with a negligible impact on the LHC operations.
the CMS dataflows are now well understood by our computing centres and that they are able to cope with the data processing and analysis operations required by the challenge.
